_readme: URL map for scripts/results.py: where the VEC's public results pages are. Each profile lists the page address patterns;
{base} is the profile's base, {slug} the district or region id as the VEC writes it ('albert-park', 'eastern-victoria').
Every run also reads the results index page ({base}) and uses the address each district and region link there has, and each
district page's own links to its voting-centre and 2CP pages, so an address that doesn't follow a pattern is still read;
'overrides' ('district:<id>' or 'region:<id>' -> full URL) beats both, for a page the index doesn't link.
The 2026 base was null until the VEC published its 2026 results pages on 28 Nov 2026 (checked 26 Nov 2026: https://www.vec.vic.gov.au/results/state-election-results
lists 2022 back to 2006 and by-elections only; .../2026-state-election-results and .../2026-state-election return 404). Until then each
run looks at 'discover.page' for a link whose text matches 'discover.link_text' and, if it finds one, uses it as the base for that run
with a ::warning::; put that address in 'base' then, and run 'python scripts/results.py --check-urls' (all 96 pages must answer).
'2022' points at the final 2022 pages and tests the parser end to end ('--profile 2022 --data-dir <copy>'). 'template-2026' is the
VEC's newest results template, the 2026 Nepean by-election (one district, read through its override): run it the same way to check
the parsers against the layout the 2026 pages are most likely to use.

2026._note: Filled 28 Nov 2026, 7 pm: the VEC published the 2026 results under /results/2026-results, with districts listed on district-election-page and regions on region-election-page (capitalised addresses, e.g. Albert-Park-District-results), so both are index pages; runs follow the links on them, and each district page's own links to its voting-centre pages. The patterns here are a fallback only (they lower-case the slug).
